instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a “lobbyist” by being employed/contracting for or receiving economic consideration and (if duties not exclusively lobbying) making lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period, but it sets no dollar compensation threshold.

The definition of “lobbyist” contains no lobbyist-side spending/expenditure trigger for registration, relying instead on employment/economic consideration and (in some cases) a 5-days communication standard.

Wisconsin requires principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements and specifies certain aggregation/itemization rules, but it does not set a per-item de minimis threshold below which expenditures need not be itemized on a lobbyist spending report.

A principal must register once aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $500 in a calendar year, and principals anticipating aggregate nonexempt lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing/registration/reporting if true.

The statute provides a 5-days communication test for lobbyist status and excludes certain low-hour non-lobbyist employees from principals’ expense reporting, but it does not create a lobbyist’s own percentage-of-compensated-time exemption from filing disclosure.
